name: linux_ptrace
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread and uap points to the Linux ptrace arguments (req, pid, addr, data). Postcondition: dispatches on uap->req and returns an errno (0 when the selected sub-operation succeeded). TRACEME, POKETEXT, POKEDATA, KILL and ATTACH are passed to kern_ptrace; DETACH, SINGLESTEP and CONT are passed with addr (void *)1 and the signal mapped by map_signum. PEEKTEXT/PEEKDATA call kern_ptrace and, only if it returned 0, copy an l_int-sized td_retval to uap->data; td_retval[0] is restored in every case. GETREGS and GETFPREGS call kern_ptrace into a local BSD buffer, convert and copyout to uap->data; SETREGS and SETFPREGS copyin from uap->data, convert and call kern_ptrace; a copyin/copyout failure is returned. GETFPXREGS/SETFPXREGS (SET first copies in; its failure is returned): EIO on a size mismatch of linux_pt_fpxreg and savexmm (a message is printed once); ESRCH when pfind finds no process; with the process locked, ESRCH if exiting, the p_candebug error, EINVAL for a system process, EPERM if not traced, EBUSY if p_pptr is not the caller or the process is not stopped and waited for; each of these exits unlocks p. Otherwise the first thread's FP/XMM registers are read (then copied out) or written (after masking mxcsr with 0xffbf) through linux_proc_read_fpxregs/linux_proc_write_fpxregs, with a hold on the process and the process lock released before the copyout. PEEKUSR/POKEUSR start with EIO and stop there if uap->addr is negative or not l_int aligned or lies in neither the linux_pt_reg range nor [LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET, LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET+LINUX_DBREG_SIZE]; in the register range they use PT_GETREGS (PEEK copies the l_int at that offset to uap->data; POKE stores (l_int)uap->data, the value itself, then PT_SETREGS); in the debug range uap->addr is reduced by LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET and PT_GETDBREGS/PT_SETDBREGS are used the same way. LINUX_PTRACE_SYSCALL and any other request print a message and return EINVAL.
note: Read sys/i386/linux/linux_ptrace_machdep.c:234-470 in full; every return is the single return(error) at 469; fail: label at 399 unlocks p. Reviewer (POKEUSR does not copy in from uap->data) is right: lines 427-428 and 452-453 use uap->data directly; prose corrected. Slice cut the head; name is the real function.

name: systrace_args
prose: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t slots large enough for the arguments of sysnum, n_args points to a writable int, and for a syscall number that takes arguments params points to that syscall's argument structure. Postcondition: the function (void) switches on sysnum; for a case with arguments the fields of the argument structure are stored in order into slots 0, 1, ... of uarg and *n_args is set to the argument count; fields typed as pointers are stored as (intptr_t) through uarg, and the generator stores some integer-like fields (for example int, clockid_t and l_size_t such as ssize in case 414) through the int64_t alias iarg and others (for example uint32_t nfds in case 414, u_int, size_t) through uarg, so the choice follows the generated per-field code and not a single rule. Cases for syscalls without arguments (and the default branch) set *n_args to 0 and write nothing to uarg, and params is not read for those. The function returns nothing and changes no state other than uarg and *n_args.
note: Generated function systrace_args (sys/i386/linux/linux_systrace_args.c:10-3362); slice 3011-3311 is mid-body (cases 403-4xx), slice cut the head. Reviewer is right that l_uint/l_size_t fields in this range (e.g. case 414 line 3113, ssize stored via iarg) go through iarg; prose rewritten. Did not read every one of the ~416 cases; read head, tail, and samples (cases 1-4, 403-404, 414, 449-452).

name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
prose: Precondition: sysnum is a syscall number, ndx an argument index, desc a writable buffer of descsz bytes. Postcondition: the function starts with p == NULL; for a sysnum case in its big switch it sets p to a constant string naming the type of argument ndx (for example "l_int") when ndx matches a case of the inner switch, and leaves p NULL otherwise (including for a sysnum with no case, a no-argument syscall or an ndx beyond the last argument); at the end, only if p is not NULL, it copies the string into desc with strlcpy truncated to descsz. It returns nothing, and desc is not touched when p is NULL.
note: Slice cut the head: real function is systrace_entry_setargdesc (sys/i386/linux/linux_systrace_args.c:3364-8742); prior name linux_syscall_argtype does not exist in the file. Read head (3364-3380), tail (8725-8742) and the sample at 8128-8140 (case 394); did not read the individual case tables.

name: systrace_args
prose: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t slots large enough for the arguments of sysnum, n_args points to a writable int, and for a syscall number that takes arguments params points to that syscall's argument structure. Postcondition: the function (void) switches on sysnum; for a case with arguments the fields are stored in order into slots 0, 1, ... of uarg and *n_args is set to the argument count; pointer fields are stored as (intptr_t) through uarg, and the generator stores each other field either through the int64_t alias iarg (for example int and several l_* typed fields) or through uarg (for example u_int and uint32_t), following the type comment of the generated line, so unsigned-looking types are not uniformly stored through uarg. Cases for syscalls without arguments, and the default branch, set *n_args to 0 and write no slot. The function returns nothing and changes only uarg and *n_args.
note: Generated function systrace_args (linux_systrace_args.c:10-3362); slice 904-1204 is mid-body, slice cut the head. Reviewer is right: l_ulong etc. go through iarg (see 3113-3120 for the same pattern); prose rewritten. Did not read each case.

name: hostap_input
prose: Precondition: ni is a valid node (non-NULL, asserted) with valid ni_vap and ni_ic, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame, rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type (the value is held in a uint8_t, initially -1 so it returns 255 when the frame was rejected before the type was read, e.g. too short or bad version), and in the paths that reach the common exit (label out, or err then out) the mbuf, if still non-NULL, is radiotap-tapped when it was not already tapped and the vap is tapping, and then freed with m_freem. Frames flagged M_AMPDU_MPDU skip validation and jump into the data path at resubmit_ampdu. Otherwise too-short frames, a bad version (goes to err), a wrong BSSID while not scanning, and failed sequence checks are dropped with statistics. Data frames are dropped (some via err, which also counts an interface input error, others via out without it) for wrong direction, unassociated or unknown source, unauthorized 4-address frames, privacy off with a protected frame, crypto decap/demic failure, defrag not complete, decap failure, unauthorized port with non-EAPOL, or unencrypted frames when DROPUNENC is set. 4-address frames from a node without a WDS vap are handed to ieee80211_dwds_discover and the function returns the type without freeing m itself. A-MPDU reorder that takes the frame, decap_amsdu or decap_fastframe returning NULL return the data type directly without the common exit. Successful data frames are delivered to ni->ni_wdsvap (4-address with a WDS vap) or hostap_deliver_data and the function returns IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA without freeing. Management frames are checked for direction, length, multicast source and protection, optionally decrypted, tapped, passed to iv_recv_mgmt and then fall to out where m is freed; control frames matching the vap go to iv_recv_ctl and then to out; an unknown type falls into err.
note: Read hostap_input in full (sys/net80211/ieee80211_hostap.c:467-908). Reviewer right: the wrong-direction data path (608) goes to out, not err, so no if_ierrors increment (err at 899-900 counts IFCOUNTER_IERRORS). Slice cut the head. Returns: 655, 799, 804, 811 are direct, 907 is the common exit. The mgmt path frees m at out after iv_recv_mgmt (885).

name: hostap_auth_shared
prose: Precondition: ni is a node whose vap is in IEEE80211_S_RUN (asserted), frm..efrm bounds the information elements of a received authentication frame, seq and status come from that frame. Postcondition: returns nothing. If privacy is disabled it goes to bad with status IEEE80211_STATUS_ALG without counting an error; if ni_authmode is neither AUTO nor SHARED it counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (ALG); only the first information element (if frm+1 < efrm) is examined: if its length overruns efrm it counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (CHALLENGE), if its id is the challenge element it is taken as the challenge. For seq CHALLENGE or RESPONSE a missing challenge or a challenge length other than IEEE80211_CHALLENGE_LEN counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (CHALLENGE). For seq REQUEST the node is duplicated from vap->iv_bss when ni is the bss (returns silently if the dup fails) or referenced if not already AREF; AREF and ASSOCID are set, RSSI and noise updated, a challenge buffer allocated (returns silently on failure) and filled with random bytes; if a RADIUS ACL policy is in force it only calls ieee80211_notify_node_auth and returns without sending a response; otherwise an auth response with seq+1 is sent. For seq RESPONSE it returns silently when ni is the bss; goes to bad (CHALLENGE) when no challenge is recorded (counting is_rx_bad_auth) or on mismatch (counting is_rx_auth_fail); on match it authorizes the node and sends an auth response with seq+1. Any other seq counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad with status SEQUENCE. The bad label calls ieee80211_send_error with (seq+1) and the status.
note: Read ieee80211_hostap.c:988-1175 in full. Reviewer claims right on both rounds: RADIUS ACL path returns after notify without a response (1117-1125); disabled privacy goes to bad (1007-1013) without incrementing is_rx_bad_auth/is_rx_auth_fail. Slice 871-1171 ends before the end of the function.

name: ieee80211_ampdu_reorder
prose: Precondition: ni is an HT node, m is an A-MPDU frame (M_AMPDU set, M_AMPDU_MPDU clear; both asserted) whose first mbuf holds the QoS header, rxs may supply A-MSDU flags. Postcondition: returns 0 (PROCESS, caller keeps m and handles it) or 1 (CONSUMED, caller must not touch m). Returns 0 without changing state when the frame is not QoS data, when addr1 is multicast, or when the TID's reorder state does not have IEEE80211_AGGR_XCHGPEND set. A frame with fragment bits in the sequence field is counted (is_ampdu_rx_drop), freed, and returns 1. Otherwise rxa_nframes is incremented, and if WAITRX was set it is cleared and the window start taken from the frame. If the frame's sequence equals rxa_start: with frames already queued, the frame is dispatched and the queue dispatched and it returns 1; with none queued it advances rxa_start by one (unless it is an A-MSDU subframe that is not the last, in which case the window is not advanced) and returns 0. If the frame lies inside the window (offset < rxa_wnd) and queued frames are older than ieee80211_ampdu_age, the queue is flushed (counted in is_ampdu_rx_age), the window start is advanced as above and it returns 0; otherwise the frame is stored in its slot (starting the age timer when the queue was empty) and it returns 1. If the offset is beyond the window but below IEEE80211_SEQ_BA_RANGE, is_ampdu_rx_move is counted, frames below rxseq - rxa_wnd + 1 are flushed with ampdu_rx_flush_upto and the sequence is re-examined from the top. Beyond that range the frame is counted dropped, freed, and it returns 1.
note: Read ieee80211_ht.c:1000-1220 in full plus ampdu_rx_flush_upto (940-986). Slice cut the head: real name ieee80211_ampdu_reorder. Returns at 1026,1036,1045,1059,1085,1101,1163,1174,1216. Part not read: ampdu_dispatch/ampdu_rx_add_slot/ampdu_rx_dispatch bodies (callee internals).

name: ieee80211_recv_bar
prose: Precondition: ni is a node and m0 holds a received BAR control frame (header at least ieee80211_frame_bar sized; the frame is not otherwise validated, see the XXX at 1245). Postcondition: returns nothing and does not free m0. If ieee80211_recv_bar_ena is clear, or the BAR's TID has no pending BA exchange (IEEE80211_AGGR_XCHGPEND clear), it increments is_ampdu_bar_bad and returns with the reorder state unchanged. Otherwise it increments is_ampdu_bar_rx; if the BAR's sequence number equals the window start it returns with nothing else changed. Otherwise, when the offset from the window start is below IEEE80211_SEQ_BA_RANGE it increments is_ampdu_bar_move and calls ampdu_rx_flush_upto(ni, rap, rxseq), which dispatches queued MSDUs with sequence numbers before rxseq (it may continue past rxseq while a contiguous run of queued frames follows) and moves the window start; if the offset was at least rxa_wnd it then sets rxa_start to rxseq explicitly. An offset at or beyond the range is counted in is_ampdu_bar_oow, noted in the node's rx_drop statistic, and leaves the window unchanged.
note: Read ieee80211_ht.c:1222-1300. Reviewer (rounds 2 and 15): flush is to rxseq, not rxseq - wnd + 1, up to but not including rxseq: right (call at 1276 passes rxseq); the earlier prose was wrong. Equal-sequence BAR returns at 1260-1261 without flush: right.

name: hwmp_recv_prep
prose: Precondition: vap has mesh and HWMP state, ni is the neighbour the PREP arrived from, wh is the received frame header and prep a parsed PREP element. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns early with no route change when the PREP's originator address is not our own address (or is a proxied route not proxied by us) and mesh forwarding (IEEE80211_MESHFLAGS_FWD) is off. It looks up or adds the route to prep_targetaddr (counting is_mesh_rtaddfailed and returning if the add fails). If that route is already VALID it returns without updating when the PREP's target sequence is older than hr_seq, or when it is not newer than hr_seq and the new metric (prep_metric plus the path metric of ni) is greater than the route's metric. Otherwise the route's sequence, next hop (ni_macaddr), metric, hop count (prep_hopcount + 1) and lifetime are set, DISCOVER is cleared and VALID set, and hwmp_update_transmitter is called. If the originator is not us and ttl > 1 and hopcount < hs_maxhops, the PREP is forwarded with hop count and metric increased and ttl decreased through hwmp_send_prep to the originator route's next hop, but the function returns without sending when no route to the originator exists (which also skips the steps below). If the AE flag is set, a proxy route for the external target address is found or added (returning with is_mesh_rtaddfailed counted if the add fails) and its fields overwritten with flags PROXY|VALID, gate = prep_targetaddr, next hop = wh->i_addr2. Finally frames staged for the target (or external) address are taken from ic_stageq and each is passed to ieee80211_vap_xmitpkt.
note: Read ieee80211_hwmp.c:1271-1479. Reviewer claims right: the discard condition (1299-1301) drops any non-local originator when FWD is off even if proxied by us, and acceptance leaves several early returns (1339, 1346, 1390, 1422) that skip later updates/queue flush; prose rewritten from the return list (1305,1325,1339,1346,1390,1422, end).

name: ieee80211_parse_beacon
prose: Precondition: ni and m are valid, m's first mbuf holds an 802.11 management header followed by a beacon or probe-response body, rxchan is the receive channel, scan is writable. The pointers stored in scan point into m's data, so they are valid only while that data is unchanged. Postcondition: the function returns scan->status. If fewer than 12 bytes follow the header it sets scan->status to IEEE80211_BPARSE_BADIELEN and returns, leaving the rest of scan as it was. Otherwise scan is zeroed and filled with tstamp (pointer), bintval, capinfo, bchan, chan (initially bchan), ies and ies_len; the information elements are then walked and pointers or values recorded per element id (ssid, rates, xrates, country, csa, quiet, tim and timoff, erp as a value, ht/vht/rsn/mesh elements, vendor WPA/WME/Atheros/TDMA elements, and the pre-draft HT vendor elements if IEEE80211_FHT_HTCOMPAT is set), with fhdwell/fhindex/erp stored as values, chan taken from the FH or DS parameter element, and unknown ids counted in is_rx_elem_unknown. If an element's length overruns the frame, the walk returns BADIELEN at that point with scan zeroed and only partly filled. After a complete walk status bits are or-ed for invalid rates, xrates, ssid, mesh id, bad beacon interval, an off-channel mismatch (chan != bchan on a non-FH phy), and a CSA element of the wrong length; a too-short country element, HT or VHT element is not flagged but its pointer is set to NULL. Status 0 means no problem was detected.
note: Read ieee80211_input.c:515-784. Reviewer right: IE-overrun return (564-565) happens after memset at 554 so scan is partly filled, not unmodified; erp (620), fhdwell/fhindex (584,586) are values. Only the <12-byte early return (552-553) leaves scan untouched except status. Note (671) sets scan->htcap, not htinfo, for the vendor htinfo case; slice cut the head.

name: setcurchan
prose: Precondition: vap is a valid vap with valid iv_ic and iv_bss, and c is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC or a channel of the com. Postcondition: if c is not ANYC it returns EBUSY for a radar channel; on a HOSTAP vap EINVAL for a NOHOSTAP channel or a channel inconsistent with iv_des_mode; on an IBSS vap EINVAL for a NOADHOC channel; and 0 without storing anything when the vap is in RUN or SLEEP state and iv_bss->ni_chan already equals c. Otherwise vap->iv_des_chan is set to c, and: for a monitor vap with a real channel, if the interface is up and running the com channel is switched with ieee80211_setcurchan and iv_bss->ni_chan updated, else ic_curchan and the rate table are set directly; for other vaps, if the vap is up and running and iv_roaming is AUTO (IS_UP_AUTO) a transition to IEEE80211_S_SCAN is requested, otherwise (when c is not ANYC) ic_curchan and the rate table are set directly. It then returns 0 (the local error stays 0 on all paths that reach the end).
note: Read ieee80211_ioctl.c:2001-2058 and IS_UP_AUTO (62-64: up+running AND iv_roaming == AUTO). Reviewers right in both rounds: early return 0 at 2019-2021 without setting iv_des_chan; scan only when IS_UP_AUTO (2045), else direct apply if a real channel (2047-2055). Slice cut the head. Did not read check_mode_consistency.

name: ieee80211_ioctl_setappie_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the com lock of vap->iv_ic (asserted with IEEE80211_LOCK_ASSERT) and fc0 selects an application IE slot; ireq gives the length and user data. Postcondition: the function does not release the lock. It switches on the subtype in fc0: BEACON (HOSTAP or IBSS vap only, else EINVAL) replaces iv_appie_beacon through setappie and, if that returned 0, calls ieee80211_beacon_notify(IEEE80211_BEACON_APPIE); PROBE_RESP and PROBE_REQ replace their slots; ASSOC_RESP (HOSTAP only) and ASSOC_REQ (STA only) replace theirs, else EINVAL; the WPA appie subtype replaces iv_appie_wpa, and when that succeeded iv_wpa_ie and iv_rsn_ie are cleared and re-derived from the new blob (setwparsnie, which checks the lengths of up to two IEs), after which the result is ENETRESET on a HOSTAP or IBSS vap (including when the appie was deleted with i_len 0). Any other subtype returns EINVAL. setappie itself returns 0 (with i_len 0 deleting and freeing the old IE), EINVAL when i_len is nonzero but outside 2..IEEE80211_MAX_APPIE, ENOMEM when allocation fails, or a copyin error, in which case the old IE is left in place. The function returns that error value.
note: Read ieee80211_ioctl.c:2387-2517. Reviewers right: setappie errors propagate (EINVAL for bad i_len, ENOMEM, copyin), ENETRESET also for WPA delete on HOSTAP/IBSS (2499-2509); EOPNOTSUPP is never returned here.

name: ieee80211_ioctl_set80211
prose: Precondition: vap and ireq are valid, and for request types that take user data ireq->i_data points to a user buffer of ireq->i_len bytes. Postcondition: the function switches on ireq->i_type; each case validates and applies one configuration item and the function returns an errno. Many cases return directly (EINVAL for out-of-range values, EOPNOTSUPP when the capability is missing), skipping the post-processing; the others leave a value in error and fall to the tail. Several cases copy data in with copyin (SSID, WEP key, BSSID, ...) and return its error (e.g. EFAULT). Many cases delegate to helpers (channel, key, MLME, scan request, WME, appie, txparams, regdomain and others), whose errno values are propagated; unknown types go to ieee80211_ioctl_setdefault, which returns EINVAL if no registered handler accepts the type. The old IEEE80211_IOC_SCAN_REQ (23) case starts a scan or moves an INIT vap into SCAN and ignores the return value of ieee80211_start_scan. After the switch, an error of ERESTART becomes the result of vap->iv_reset when the interface is up and running and 0 otherwise, and an error of ENETRESET calls ieee80211_init when the vap is up with auto roaming, and is then replaced by 0. So ENETRESET and ERESTART are not returned to the caller; EINPROGRESS can be returned from the scan request path.
note: Whole function is 2770-3587 (about 800 lines, switch over ~100 request types); read 2770-2960, the scan cases 3060-3100, and the tail 3555-3587 plus the return/goto/error list of 2960-3555; did not read the bodies of the individual cases beyond that, and none of the delegated helpers (partly read). Reviewer round 15 is mixed: the OLD_IEEE80211_IOC_SCAN_REQ case at 3067-3087 does ignore ieee80211_start_scan return (so that sentence is true of this function), but the ENETRESET/ERESTART conversion at 3577-3585 and direct returns were missing from the prior prose. Reviewer round 1 (copyin errors, subhandler errors) right. Whether EINPROGRESS can come through scanreq: ieee80211_scanreq returns EINPROGRESS at 2678 and is called from ieee80211_ioctl_scanreq (2699) at 3090.

name: mesh_input
prose: Precondition: ni is a valid node on a mesh vap, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame whose ownership passes to the function, and the TX lock is not held (asserted). Postcondition: returns the frame type held in a uint8_t (initially -1, so 255 when the frame was rejected before the type was read, i.e. too short or bad version), or IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA from two paths. The inactivity timer is reloaded first. Frames shorter than the minimum header or with a bad version are dropped (the bad-version one counts an interface input error); while not scanning, RSSI and noise are updated and for sequenced frames a failed duplicate check drops the frame. Data frames: dropped if ni is the vap's bss node, if the peer link is not ESTABLISHED, for a direction other than FROMDS or DSTODS (counts an input error), for a non-QoS subtype or missing mesh-control bit (input error), after defragmentation fails, when the mesh source address taken from addr3 or addr4 equals our own address, when mesh_checkpseq reports a duplicate; otherwise the frame is routed to mesh_recv_indiv_data_to_me, mesh_recv_group_data or mesh_recv_indiv_data_to_fwrd, whose negative result counts an error and positive result drops the frame without that count, and a zero result goes on to radiotap, mesh_decap (a NULL result is dropped, without an error count for null-data subtypes), optional A-MSDU decap (returning DATA when it yields NULL), and ieee80211_deliver_data, after which the function returns the type without freeing m. Management frames are checked for direction and length, protected frames are discarded, and others are handed to iv_recv_mgmt and then fall to out. Control frames are counted and dropped. Unknown types go to the error exit. At the common exit (err then out) a still-owned m is tapped to radiotap if it was not yet tapped and then freed with m_freem.
note: Slice cut the head: real function mesh_input, ieee80211_mesh.c:1541-1841, read in full. Prior prose said it "always returns the decoded type" including the success path; real returns: 1782 (DATA after A-MSDU NULL), 1785 (type), 1838 (type, possibly the 255 sentinel). Not read: mesh_recv_* helpers, mesh_decap (callee internals).

name: ieee80211_beacon_update
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold the com lock (the function takes and releases it), ni and m describe an already-constructed beacon whose offsets in the vap's beacon-offsets structure match the mbuf, and the mbuf has contiguous room for a maximal TIM bitmap and for a CSA element. Postcondition: the com lock is taken on entry and released before each of the four returns. It returns 1 immediately, after rebuilding the whole beacon with ieee80211_beacon_construct, when the CSA flag is set and the vap's CSA count equals ic_csa_count (the vap's count is reset, and ieee80211_csa_completeswitch is called first if ic_csa_newchan is set), or when the QUIET_IE flag state differs from iv_quiet (the flag is toggled to match). Otherwise it assigns the beacon sequence number, rewrites the capability field, handles WME aggressive-mode switching and the WME element, HT info, TDMA and mesh beacon updates, and for HOSTAP/MBSS vaps updates the TIM (moving the trailing elements and the stored offsets when the bitmap length changes, which sets the return value to 1), counts the DTIM countdown and the multicast bit, inserts the CSA element when the vap's CSA count is 0 (growing the mbuf lengths, without setting the return value) or decrements its count otherwise, adds the quiet element when DFS and quiet apply, and updates ERP and Atheros elements when flagged. A pending APPIE update that changes the application IE length moves the trailer and sets the return value to 1. The function returns 1 if the beacon length changed by those TIM or APPIE adjustments and 0 otherwise.
note: Slice cut the head: real function ieee80211_beacon_update, ieee80211_output.c:3786-4119, read in full. Reviewer (round 15) right: CSA insertion (4038-4060) grows m_len but does not set len_changed, and the CSA flag is deliberately not cleared (4064). Four returns: 3821, 3843, 3857, 4118. Not read: ieee80211_beacon_construct and the add_* helpers.

name: ieee80211_csa_cancelswitch
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the com lock (checked with IEEE80211_LOCK_ASSERT); the function does not check that a channel switch is actually pending. Postcondition: it calls the static csa_completeswitch, which sets ic_csa_newchan to NULL, clears IEEE80211_F_CSAPENDING and moves every vap currently in IEEE80211_S_CSA to IEEE80211_S_RUN through ieee80211_new_state_locked (vaps in other states are left alone). Unlike ieee80211_csa_completeswitch it does not call ieee80211_setcurchan and does not update any vap's iv_bss->ni_chan, so the current channel and BSS channels are not changed by this function. It returns nothing.
note: Read ieee80211_proto.c:2329-2381. Reviewers right in both rounds: cancel does not set channels (completeswitch does at 2362-2365, cancel only calls csa_completeswitch at 2380), and no pending check exists, only the lock assert.

name: ieee80211_alloc_countryie
prose: Precondition: ic is a valid com with a valid ic_bsschan, channel table (ic_channels, ic_nchans) and regdomain. Postcondition: returns a newly allocated zeroed ieee80211_appie owned by the caller (to be freed with IEEE80211_FREE), or NULL after printing a message when the allocation of IEEE80211_COUNTRY_MAX_SIZE bytes fails (the only NULL return). The country element's id is IEEE80211_ELEMID_COUNTRY, its country code is rd->isocc, or two blanks (with a message printed) when isocc[0] is '\0', and its third character is 'I' or 'O' when rd->location says so and a blank otherwise. The channel table is walked once: channels whose ic_ieee was already seen (duplicates) or whose flags match the skip set for the BSS channel's mode and band (turbo, half/quarter, the other band, and for FH also OFDM/CCK/DYN) are ignored; each remaining channel starts a new run of (first channel, count 1, ic_maxregpower) unless its number is the one after the previous channel and its maxregpower equals that of the current run, in which case the run's count is incremented. If a new run would exceed IEEE80211_COUNTRY_MAX_BANDS a message is printed and the loop stops, so the element is truncated. The element length is set from the data written, padded with one zero byte when odd, and ie_len is set to the total size.
note: Slice cut the head: real function ieee80211_alloc_countryie, ieee80211_regdomain.c:232-340, read in full. Returns: 271 (NULL on alloc failure), 338 (aie). frm[-1] at 312 reads the previous maxregpower (or the location byte on the first iteration, where nextchan=0 makes it a new run anyway).

name: sta_roam_check
prose: Precondition: vap is a station vap (the sole caller sta_age checks this) with valid iv_ic and iv_bss, ss->ss_priv is the sta_table, and the vap's iv_roamparms rate and rssi for the phymode of ic_bsschan are nonzero (KASSERT). Postcondition: returns nothing. If the scan cache has no entry for the BSS node's MAC address it returns with nothing changed. Otherwise it takes the roam thresholds for the BSS channel's mode, the current RSSI from ic_node_getrssi, and the current rate (the node's tx rate when the unicast rate is not fixed, else a value equal to the roam rate so the rate test cannot fire). Only when the current rate is below the roam rate or the current RSSI is below the roam RSSI (either one is enough) does it go on: if the scan cache is older than iv_scanvalid it may start a background scan (not when the current channel is dynamic turbo, and only with scan offload or after iv_bgscanidle of no data) and returns without selecting; otherwise it stores the current RSSI into the matching cache entry's se_rssi, runs select_bss, and when that returns a different entry it calls ieee80211_sta_join on that entry's channel (demoted from 11g to 11b when STA_DEMOTE11B is set) and ignores the join result. In all other cases nothing further is modified.
note: Read ieee80211_scan_sta.c:1341-1414. Reviewers right: the condition at 1381 is "curRate < roamRate || curRssi < roamRssi" (either, not both); se_rssi is written at 1397 before select_bss, so state may change even when no join follows.

name: sta_add
prose: Precondition: the caller does not hold the scan-table lock; ss, curchan, sp, wh, subtype, rssi and noise describe one received beacon or probe response from wh->i_addr2, with sp->rates non-NULL and sp->rates[1] (and sp->xrates[1] if xrates is non-NULL) at most IEEE80211_RATE_MAXSIZE, and when the chosen channel is VHT or HT but the frame lacks the corresponding capability a non-VHT or non-HT channel with the same frequency must exist (the KASSERTs would fire otherwise). Postcondition: returns 0 with the table lock released when allocation of a new entry fails and nothing was inserted; otherwise it returns 1 after the lock is released. The table entry for the sender MAC is found or created (zeroed, appended to the list and hash bucket, RSSI average at the dummy marker) and updated: ssid (copied when the new ssid is non-empty and the frame is a probe response or the entry has no ssid), rates, extended rates (length cleared when absent), bssid from addr3, on-channel RSSI average and noise (not updated when the frame was off-channel), timestamp, beacon interval, capability info, mesh id if present. se_chan is set to curchan for an on-channel frame; for an off-channel frame it is set to the channel found from sp->chan, else kept if already set, else set to curchan. It is then demoted to a non-VHT channel if the frame has no VHT capability and then to a non-HT channel if it has no HT capability. FH, ERP, TIM offset, DTIM period and country code are copied; a country mismatch with 11d active triggers at most one notification per scan generation; the IEs are copied with ieee80211_ies_init (its result ignored); the failure count is cleared after STA_FAILS_AGE; last-update time, se_seen and not-seen count are updated and st_maxrssi for the beacon channel raised. After unlocking, if PICK1ST is set and no pick has yet been made and match_bss accepts the entry, IEEE80211_SCAN_GOTPICK is set.
note: Slice cut the head: real function sta_add (ieee80211_scan_sta.c:235-421; the packet name sta_update does not exist), read in full. Reviewer right: the off-channel fallback to curchan applies only when se_chan is NULL (323-326); an existing entry keeps its old channel.

name: tdma_update
prose: Precondition: vap is a TDMA vap (IEEE80211_C_TDMA set in iv_caps, asserted), tdma points to a received TDMA parameter element, ni is the sending node. The function takes no reference on ni. Postcondition: returns 0, with no runtime state, beacon, driver callback or join/leave notification changed (apart from the rate-limited diagnostic bookkeeping in tdma_lastprint/tdma_fails), when the received slot count, slot length (le16toh(tdma_slotlen)*100) or beacon interval differs from the current value and is not valid, or when pickslot is nonzero and no free slot above 0 is found in the in-use bitmap (a message is printed). Otherwise it computes which of slot count, slot length, beacon interval and slot differ (the slot is changed only when pickslot is nonzero and the picked slot, the highest free one, differs; with pickslot zero ts->tdma_slot is unchanged), forces all four updates when ni is not the current peer, stores the changed values and calls ieee80211_beacon_notify(IEEE80211_BEACON_TDMA) when any changed, calls ic_tdma_update(ni, tdma, update) only if the vap is in RUN state, and when ni differs from ts->tdma_peer calls ieee80211_notify_node_leave on vap->iv_bss (only if a previous peer was recorded, and on iv_bss, not on that peer), then ieee80211_notify_node_join(ni, 1) and records ni as the peer. It then returns 1.
note: Read ieee80211_tdma.c:409-518 in full. Reviewers right: leave notification targets vap->iv_bss (512), and with pickslot == 0 the slot is not taken from tdma (450, 466-467, 486-487). Returns: 426, 436, 446, 464, 517.

name: ieee80211_create_wds
prose: Precondition: vap has IEEE80211_F_DESBSSID set and is in IEEE80211_S_RUN state (both KASSERTs), with iv_des_bssid holding the peer address. Postcondition: in non-legacy mode (IEEE80211_FEXT_WDSLEGACY clear) it looks up the node for iv_des_bssid in the station table under the node-table lock; if none is found ni stays NULL and nothing is linked; if the found node already has ni_wdsvap set (to any vap, possibly this one) it is left untouched and nothing is linked; otherwise the vap's bss is replaced with that node through iv_update_bss, ni_wdsvap is set to vap, and after unlocking the previous bss node is freed. In legacy mode a new WDS node for iv_des_bssid on chan is created with ieee80211_node_create_wds; if that succeeds it is installed as the vap's bss (with an extra reference, flag AREF set, the old bss freed), the driver ic_newassoc and the authenticator's ia_node_join are called when present, the node is authorized only if its ni_authmode is not IEEE80211_AUTH_8021X, and a join notification is sent. In both modes, when ni is non-NULL wds_flush is then called to send pending frames for it. It returns ENOENT when ni is NULL (node not found in non-legacy mode, node creation failed in legacy mode) and 0 otherwise, including the non-legacy case where a node was found but owned by another WDS vap and no link was made.
note: Read ieee80211_wds.c:122-223 in full. Reviewers right: the found-but-in-use branch (161-173) links nothing yet returns 0 (ni != NULL at 222); ENOENT also covers legacy create failure; legacy authorization is conditional (209-210).

name: wds_input
prose: Precondition: ni is the WDS peer node (non-NULL, asserted) of a WDS vap, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame whose ownership passes to the function, rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type held in a uint8_t (initially -1, so 255 when rejected before the type was read), or IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA from some data paths. Frames flagged M_AMPDU_MPDU skip validation and enter the data path at resubmit_ampdu. Otherwise: frames shorter than the minimum header are dropped; ni_inact is reloaded for a non-multicast addr1; a bad version goes to the error exit (counts an interface input error); frames shorter than a 4-address header, or whose addr1 is neither our address nor the broadcast address are dropped; RSSI and noise are updated and for sequenced frames a failed rx-sequence check drops the frame. Data frames are dropped if the direction is not DSTODS, if the vap is not in legacy WDS mode, after A-MPDU reorder consumes the frame, for privacy off with a protected frame, crypto decap or demic failure, incomplete defragmentation, decap failure (error exit, except null-data subtypes), an unauthorized port with non-EAPOL, or an unencrypted frame when IEEE80211_F_DROPUNENC applies; A-MSDU or fast-frame decap returning NULL returns the DATA type directly; otherwise the frame is delivered with ieee80211_deliver_data and the function returns the DATA type without freeing it. Management frames are counted, checked for direction, length and protection, handed to iv_recv_mgmt, and then freed at the common exit; control frames are counted and freed; unknown types go to the error exit. At the common exit a non-NULL m is tapped to radiotap if not yet tapped and freed.
note: Slice cut the head: real function wds_input (ieee80211_wds.c:407-741), read from 420 to the end. Note: ieee80211_crypto_demic is called at 602 whether or not key is NULL (callee not read). Returns: 677, 682, 686 direct; 740 common exit.

name: ng_hci_process_command_status
prose: Precondition: unit is a valid HCI unit and e is an mbuf holding a Command_Status event; the function takes ownership of e. Postcondition: if the pullup of the ng_hci_command_status_ep header fails (the pullup macro then releases the mbuf and e is NULL) it returns ENOBUFS at once, without calling ng_hci_send_command. Otherwise it stores the controller's number of command packets in the unit buffer info; if the opcode is 0x0000 (NOOP) it skips matching; otherwise complete_command is tried (EINVAL when no command is pending, the queue is empty or the first queued opcode differs, ETIMEDOUT when the command timeout cannot be cancelled), and on success the opcode is converted to host order and dispatched by OGF: link control, link policy and LE go to process_link_control_status, process_link_policy_status and process_le_status, whose return values (which these helpers decide, and which can be other errnos) become the result and which take care of the dequeued command packet; BT_LOGO and VENDOR free it and give 0; any other OGF frees it and gives EINVAL. After the pullup succeeded, the code reaches the out label on every path of this function, where e is freed with NG_FREE_M and ng_hci_send_command(unit) is called, and the error value is returned.
note: Read ng_hci_cmds.c:268-327 and complete_command 333-385. Reviewer right (round 15): helper errors from process_*_status propagate (299-306); earlier reviewer about pullup failure is also consistent: returns at 277 before send_command (the macro frees the mbuf on failure). Did not read the process_* helpers (callee internals).

name: con_compl
prose: Precondition: unit is a valid HCI unit and event is an mbuf holding a Connection_Complete event; the function takes ownership of event. Postcondition: if the pullup of the ng_hci_con_compl_ep header fails it returns ENOBUFS (the macro having released the mbuf). Otherwise it looks for a descriptor with the same link type and address in state NG_HCI_CON_W4_CONN_COMPLETE. If none exists and ep->status is nonzero, it does nothing further and returns 0; if none exists and status is 0 a new descriptor is created (ENOMEM if that fails) and given the address. If one exists its timeout is cancelled, and a nonzero return from ng_hci_con_untimeout is returned without updating the descriptor. Otherwise the descriptor receives the connection handle and encryption mode, ng_hci_lp_con_cfm reports the status to the upper layers, and with a nonzero status the descriptor is freed, while with status 0 it becomes NG_HCI_CON_OPEN and, for an ACL link, a Write_Link_Policy_Settings command is built from the unit's features (if an mbuf can be allocated), queued, and sent when no command is pending. In every path after a successful pullup the event mbuf is freed, and the error value returned is 0 except for the ENOMEM and untimeout cases.
note: Read ng_hci_evnt.c:676-799. Reviewers right: ENOBUFS and the untimeout error (730-731) were missing from the prior prose, and no-descriptor with status != 0 returns 0 without updating anything (720-721). Slice starts mid-file; this is the function at 677.

name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_con_req_rsp
prose: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_con_op in its data and header.token identifies a socket pcb; rt is not used. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE, taking no lock, when arglen differs from sizeof(op); otherwise takes ng_btsocket_l2cap_sockets_mtx, finds the pcb by token (ENOENT if none), takes the pcb mutex, and returns ENOENT without other effects when the pcb is not in NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_CONNECTING. It then cancels the pcb timeout. For op->result NG_L2CAP_PENDING it re-arms the timeout and returns 0. For NG_L2CAP_SUCCESS: on an ATT or SMP channel it stores encryption and cid and either moves to W4_ENC_CHANGE (re-arming the timeout) when encryption is needed but absent, or to OPEN with soisconnected; on other channels it stores cid and encryption and sends a config request, and if that send fails it sends a disconnect request with token 0, sets the state to CLOSED and calls soisdisconnected and the function returns that send error, while on success it sets CFG_IN_SENT, state CONFIGURING and re-arms the timeout, returning 0. For any other result it stores the errno converted from the result in so_error, sets CLOSED and calls soisdisconnected, returning 0. Both mutexes are released before the return in all paths where they were taken.
note: Read ng_btsocket_l2cap.c:412-514. Reviewers right: SUCCESS path may close the socket and return the cfg-request error (484-491), and the non-success result path (499-509) was missing. Returns: 421, 431, 451, 461, 513.

name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_con_ind
prose: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_con_ind_ip and rt is the route the indication came from; ng_btsocket_l2cap_sockets_mtx is not held. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE immediately, with no lock taken, when arglen differs from sizeof(*ip). Otherwise it takes the sockets mutex and looks for a listening pcb by (rt->src, psm). If there is none the result code is NG_L2CAP_PSM_NOT_SUPPORTED. If there is one it creates a socket with sonewconn; failure gives result NG_L2CAP_NO_RESOURCES, success creates a new pcb whose source address is the listener's when that is not BDADDR_ANY and rt->src otherwise, with dst, psm, cid, route taken from the indication and imtu, oflow and flush_timo copied from the listener. In all these cases, ng_btsocket_l2cap_send_l2ca_con_rsp_req is then called (carrying the new pcb's token, or 0 if none, and the result, which is 0 when the new pcb was made) and its return value is the function's return value. When a new pcb was created, a send error sets its so_error, state CLOSED and soisdisconnected, and a send success sets state CONNECTING, soisconnecting and arms its timeout. The new pcb's mutex, then the listener's mutex (if taken), then the sockets mutex are released before returning.
note: Read ng_btsocket_l2cap.c:587-689. Reviewers right: on send error the new pcb is CLOSED not CONNECTING (669-673), and src is the listener src only when it is not BDADDR_ANY, else rt->src (641-644). The slice is mid-function of the same pair.

name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_cfg_rsp_rsp
prose: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_cfg_rsp_op and the caller does not hold the sockets mutex. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE (no lock taken) when arglen differs from sizeof(*op); takes the sockets mutex and finds the pcb by token (ENOENT if none), takes the pcb mutex, and returns ENOENT with no other effect if the pcb is not in NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_CONFIGURING. If op->result is not NG_L2CAP_SUCCESS it goes to the disconnect exit: the timeout is cancelled, a disconnect request with token 0 is sent, the state becomes CLOSED, soisdisconnected is called and 0 is returned. If the result is success, CFG_OUT_SENT is cleared and CFG_OUT set; if cfg_state is then CFG_BOTH the timeout is cancelled, the state becomes OPEN and soisconnected is called and it returns 0; otherwise, if CFG_IN_SENT is not yet set, an incoming-path config request is sent: on failure it takes the disconnect exit and returns that send error, on success it sets CFG_IN_SENT and returns 0; if CFG_IN_SENT is already set nothing more is done and it returns 0. The pcb and sockets mutexes are released before every return after they were taken.
note: Read ng_btsocket_l2cap.c:854-943. Reviewers right: send_cfg_req error propagates (916-918, 942) and the already-CFG_IN_SENT case is a no-op return 0 (914).

name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_raw_control
prose: Precondition: so is a socket whose raw L2CAP pcb may or may not exist, cmd is an ioctl command and data points to the command-specific structure. Postcondition: returns EINVAL before taking any lock when the pcb or the global ng_btsocket_l2cap_raw_node is NULL. Otherwise it takes the pcb mutex and returns EHOSTUNREACH if the pcb has no route, or EBUSY if pcb->token is nonzero (a request already pending; that token is left set). It then switches on cmd. GET_FLAGS, GET_DEBUG, GET_AUTO_DISCON_TIMO use the synchronous send helper and return its error; SET_DEBUG and SET_AUTO_DISCON_TIMO send a message to the route's hook only if the pcb has NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_RAW_PRIVILEGED and otherwise give EPERM; GET_INFO also requires the privileged flag (EPERM). The list and ping/info commands validate arguments (EINVAL for bad counts, NULL buffers or echo sizes; ENOMEM if the message cannot be allocated), allocate a message with a fresh token stored in pcb->token, send it to the hook, and sleep with msleep for the reply; a send error, a msleep error (including interruption or timeout) or a copyin error is returned with pcb->token cleared; a reply whose command differs from the one sent or is missing gives EINVAL; otherwise the reply data is copied out to user space (copyout errors, such as EFAULT, are returned) and the reply message is freed. In the ping case the pcb mutex is dropped around copyin and retaken. An unknown cmd gives EINVAL. In the return paths read (all of the cases up to GET_INFO and the common exit) the pcb mutex is released before returning; the function returns 0 only when the selected command's steps completed without error.
note: Whole function read for the return/unlock list (ng_btsocket_l2cap_raw.c:785-1149): read 785-1060 fully, and for 1060-1148 the return/unlock/case list only (GET_INFO and the two AUTO_DISCON_TIMO cases partly read: not read line by line). Reviewers right: EBUSY leaves token set (807-809), the NULL pcb/node EINVAL returns (793-796) occur before the lock, so the old "released on every path" claim was too broad; copyout/msleep errors are possible.

name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_receive_sabm
prose: Precondition: the caller holds s->session_mtx (asserted with mtx_assert) and dlci is the DLCI of the received SABM frame. Postcondition: for dlci 0 in session state CONNECTED or OPEN it sends a UA command; on success the session becomes OPEN and ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_cfm is called and 0 is returned, and on failure the session state is set CLOSED, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_session_clean is called and the send error is returned. For dlci 0 in any other session state it changes nothing and returns EINVAL. For dlci other than 0 it returns EINVAL, changing nothing, when the session is not OPEN. Otherwise, if a pcb with that DLCI exists: when it is not in NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CONNECTING (any other state, including DISCONNECTING) it returns ENOENT without changing it; when it is CONNECTING its timeout is cancelled, UA and then an MSC are sent, and on success the pcb becomes DLC_CONNECTED and soisconnected is called (return 0), on failure ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill(pcb, error) is called and the error returned; the pcb mutex is released before the return. If no pcb exists for the DLCI, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_ind is asked for a pcb for the server channel: if it returns one, its dlci is set and the same UA, MSC, CONNECTED or kill sequence follows (returning 0 or the error); if it returns NULL a DM command is sent and the function returns the result of that send (0 on success), with no pcb changed.
note: Read ng_btsocket_rfcomm.c:1950-2060 in full. Reviewer round 15 right: when no pcb exists and connect_ind returns NULL the function sends DM and returns that send result, so it returns 0 without moving any pcb to CONNECTED (2055-2057); dlci==0 in an invalid state returns EINVAL (1978-1983). Slice 1779-2029 holds most of the function (name at 1951).

name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_receive_sabm
prose: Precondition: the caller holds s->session_mtx (asserted with mtx_assert) and dlci is the DLCI of the received SABM frame. Postcondition: for dlci 0 in session state CONNECTED or OPEN it sends a UA command; on success the session becomes OPEN and ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_cfm is called and 0 is returned, and on failure the session state is set CLOSED, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_session_clean is called and the send error is returned. For dlci 0 in any other session state it changes nothing and returns EINVAL. For dlci other than 0 it returns EINVAL, changing nothing, when the session is not OPEN. Otherwise, if a pcb with that DLCI exists: when it is not in NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CONNECTING (any other state, including DISCONNECTING) it returns ENOENT without changing it; when it is CONNECTING its timeout is cancelled, UA and then an MSC are sent, and on success the pcb becomes DLC_CONNECTED and soisconnected is called (return 0), on failure ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill(pcb, error) is called and the error returned; the pcb mutex is released before the return. If no pcb exists for the DLCI, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_ind is asked for a pcb for the server channel: if it returns one, its dlci is set and the same UA, MSC, CONNECTED or kill sequence follows (returning 0 or the error); if it returns NULL a DM command is sent and the function returns the result of that send (0 on success), with no pcb changed.
note: Same function as the other slice (ng_btsocket_rfcomm.c:1950-2060), slice cut the head. Reviewer round 15 is wrong for this source: a pcb that is not CONNECTING (including DISCONNECTING) returns ENOENT at 2007-2013; it is not killed and does not return 0 here. Reviewer round 1 (returns 0 after a successful DM with no pcb) is right (2055-2059).

name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill
prose: Precondition: the caller holds pcb->pcb_mtx and the session mutex of pcb->session (both asserted with mtx_assert), and pcb->session is non-NULL (the function calls panic if it is NULL). Postcondition: returns nothing. Any pending DLC timeout is cancelled, the pcb is removed from the session's dlcs list and pcb->session is set to NULL, pcb->state becomes NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CLOSED, so_error is set to error, soisdisconnected is called and sleepers on pcb->state are woken. If the session's dlcs list is then empty and the session is the initiator (INITIATOR(s)): in session state CLOSED or DISCONNECTING nothing changes; in state OPEN a DISC command is sent on the multiplexor channel and, if the send succeeds, the session becomes DISCONNECTING, otherwise (and also for CONNECTING and CONNECTED) the session becomes CLOSED; any other session state calls panic. When that branch is taken ng_btsocket_rfcomm_task_wakeup is called. When dlcs is not empty or the session is not the initiator the session state is left unchanged.
note: Read ng_btsocket_rfcomm.c:3289-3358. Reviewers right: the session transition also requires INITIATOR(s) (3319) and an invalid session state panics (3350-3352), so "otherwise to CLOSED" was not true for every state. Slice cut the head.

name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect
prose: Precondition: so, nam and td come from the connect system call; the function does not hold any of the module's mutexes on entry. Postcondition: returns EINVAL if the socket has no pcb or nam is NULL, then EAFNOSUPPORT if the family is not AF_BLUETOOTH, EINVAL if the length is not sizeof(struct sockaddr_rfcomm) or the channel is above 30, EDESTADDRREQ if the channel is 0 or the destination bdaddr is BDADDR_ANY. It then creates an L2CAP socket with socreate (the result is saved in error and not checked yet), takes the sessions mutex, and looks up a session for (pcb->src, destination). With no session: if no L2CAP socket exists it returns the socreate error; otherwise it creates a session, returning its error (and closing the L2CAP socket) on failure. With an existing session the new L2CAP socket, if any, is closed. It then locks the session and pcb, computes the DLCI, and returns EBUSY if that DLCI already exists on the session. If the session state is CONNECTING, CONNECTED or OPEN, the pcb is given the destination, channel and DLCI, linked into the session, timeout armed and soisconnecting called; in session state OPEN it also takes the session mtu and source, sets the state to DLC_CONFIGURING and sends a PN command (its error, or that of the task wakeup, becomes the result and the pcb stays linked in CONFIGURING), else the state is W4_CONNECT; in the W4_CONNECT case error is not reset, so it can still hold the earlier socreate error when an existing session was found and socreate failed. Any other session state returns ECONNRESET without linking the pcb. All three mutexes are released before the final return.
note: Read ng_btsocket_rfcomm.c:491-620 in full. Reviewer round 15 right: on send_pn failure in an OPEN session the pcb state is DLC_CONFIGURING (601-605), not W4_CONNECT; round 1 right: the pcb is already linked and modified (590-601) when send_pn fails. The stale-socreate-error path (523-524, 553-554, 607) is my own finding. Note: the order is family check before length check.

name: nga_rcvmsg
prose: Precondition: node is a ng_async node whose private data is its softc sc, and item carries a control message. Postcondition: for typecookie NGM_ASYNC_COOKIE the command is handled: GET_STATS allocates a response and copies sc->stats into it (ENOMEM if the allocation fails); CLR_STATS zeroes sc->stats; GET_CONFIG allocates a response and copies sc->cfg into it (ENOMEM on failure); SET_CONFIG returns EINVAL when arglen differs from sizeof(struct ng_async_cfg) or either MRU is outside NG_ASYNC_MIN_MRU..NG_ASYNC_MAX_MRU, otherwise normalizes cfg->enabled to 0 or 1, replaces sc->abuf with a larger buffer when smru grows and sc->sbuf with a larger buffer when amru grows (ENOMEM if an allocation fails; when the second one fails the first buffer has already been replaced and sc->cfg is not updated), resets the receive mode to HUNT with slen 0 when the sync buffer is reallocated or the config is disabled, and copies the new config into sc->cfg. Any other command or cookie gives EINVAL. The code then reaches the done label (directly or through ERROUT): NG_RESPOND_MSG(error, node, item, resp) is called, with resp non-NULL only for a successful GET_STATS or GET_CONFIG, the message is freed with NG_FREE_MSG, and the variable error is returned (0 on success, otherwise the errno chosen above; the macro's own effect on error was not read).
note: Slice cut the head: real function nga_rcvmsg, ng_async.c:252-329, read in full. Reviewer: NG_RESPOND_MSG with resp NULL sends no data reply; I did not read the macro (netgraph.h), so I describe only what is passed to it, and avoid claiming whether CLR_STATS/SET_CONFIG get a reply. Return 328 is the only return.
